text.p: Morgans Gold Mines Ltd said on Tuesday an initial estimate of its Abednego nickel project in Western Australia suggested a larger and better grade resource than expected.
After two months of drilling, the resource was estimated, at a 0.5 percent nickel cut-off grade, at 100 million tonnes grading 1.09 percent nickel equivalent, Morgans said.
Within that tonnage, at a 0.8 percent cut-off grade, the resource was estimated at 53 million tonnes at 1.33 percent nickel equivalent.

The Abednego project is located near Leonora and lies adjacent to the Murrin Murrin project deposits, which are being developed by Anaconda Nickel Ltd and Glencore International AG, a Swiss metals trading company.
"The resource at this stage of appraisal is larger and of better grade than we had anticipated," said Morgans chairman Bruce Corlett in a statement.
A better estimate was expected to be available in September, he said.
